trajectory_summary: This is a short, low-energy call where the customer arrives pre-decided against solar and the rep never resets the frame. The customer discloses an existing 11-panel system and a clear cost objection, but the rep runs a partial verify question, confirms the tax-credit expiration (removing the customer's own hoped-for lever), and then exits passively without running any orphaned-flow qualifying questions or attempting a reframe.
outcome_dispute: v1 outcome is unknown/unclear; the transcript supports a likely DQ (existing 11-panel system, customer explicitly states no financial benefit) but the rep never asked the orphaned_flow qualifiers (ownership type, install company, system status, panel size) needed to confirm a hard DQ, so this should be read as a probable/likely DQ rather than a confirmed one.

observed_outcome.quote: you know, financially, it doesn't make sense to me.
observed_outcome.reasoning: The customer explicitly declines based on his own cost analysis and existing 11-panel system, and the call ends with no appointment. This reads as a likely/probable DQ rather than a confirmed hard DQ, however, since the rep never ran the orphaned_flow qualifying questions (ownership type, install company, system working status) that would formally confirm whether this is a hard disqualifier per dq_rules or a viable expansion lead.

bill_anchor_audit.reasoning: The rep captured a current bill range of $100-150/month but never used it -- he didn't flip it against the twenty-year-payback objection or connect it to the pool/spa load disclosed seconds later; the flip should have gone right after 00:55 when the customer explained the driver of that bill.

bill_document_audit.reasoning: The rep never asked for the actual utility bill document (mail/online, photo, text) at any point in the call -- he only asked for a verbal dollar range, and the call ended before any document request could occur.

interest_reason_audit.reasoning: The rep never explicitly asked 'what interested you in solar,' but the customer volunteered his reason (checking on a state tax credit) unprompted. The rep confirmed the credit expired but never pivoted to any other value angle (e.g., expansion for the pool load) once that reason was closed off.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: orphaned_flow qualifiers not run on disclosed existing system
primary_coaching_focus.quote: to making the investment. We already have 11 panels.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The moment the customer disclosed an existing 11-panel system, this became an orphaned-flow call, but the rep never asked ownership type, install company, or system status -- so Ion has no confirmed data on whether this is a hard DQ (leased/PPA) or a viable expansion lead. This is the single highest-value fix since it determines whether the call was correctly let go or a live lead was dropped.

key_moments.quote: to making the investment. We already have 11 panels.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer discloses an existing 11-panel system mid-call, which should trigger Ion's orphaned_flow line of questions (own vs. lease, install company, system size, is it working). The rep never runs any of these; he only asks about the current monthly bill.

key_moments.quote: Okay. But that's because we got a swimming pool and a spa.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer volunteers that his higher bill is driven by a pool and spa -- exactly the kind of higher-load enthusiasm signal that could justify an expansion sale (additional panels or battery) rather than a flat DQ. This is a different revenue angle than the orphaned-system DQ question: it's an upsell opening, not a qualification gate.

key_moments.quote: and that's where I found your phone number.
key_moments.stewart_read: Customer explains he was searching for New Mexico's tax credit info and that's how Ion got his number -- this is useful context (motivation was tax-credit driven, not bill-pain driven) that the rep never probes further (e.g., did he get a design/quote from anyone else when he had 11 panels installed).

key_moments.quote: Oh, okay. Yeah. I hear you. Yeah. No. Unfortunately, those have been expired since, like, I believe, the first of the year.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep confirms the tax credit is expired, which is accurate per schema's tax_credit_disclosure note about purchased systems, but he delivers it flatly and removes the customer's own reason for even considering expansion without offering the schema's stated alternative purchase-without-tax-credit option.
